title: Inhibition of Aurora-A/N-Myc Protein-Protein Interaction Using Peptidomimetics: Understanding the Role of Peptide Cyclization.
authors: Dawber, Robert S; Gimenez, Diana; Batchelor, Matthew; Miles, Jennifer A; Wright, Megan H; Bayliss, Richard; Wilson, Andrew J
journal: Chembiochem : a European journal of chemical biology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究N-Myc/Aurora-A蛋白-蛋白相互作用的拟肽抑制剂，虽涉及MD模拟，但对象为蛋白-蛋白互作而非蛋白-DNA互作，与本课题TF-DNA结合机制无直接关联。
abstract: Using N-Myc(61-89) as a starting template we showcase the systematic use of truncation and maleimide constraining to develop peptidomimetic inhibitors of the N-Myc/Aurora-A protein-protein interaction (PPI); a potential anticancer drug discovery target. The most promising of these - N-Myc(73-94-N85C/G89C-mal) - is shown to favour a more Aurora-A compliant binding ensemble in comparison to the linear wild-type sequence as observed through fluorescence anisotropy competition assays, circular dichroism (CD) and nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) experiments. Further in silico investigation of this peptide in its Aurora-A bound state, by molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, imply (i) the bound conformation is more stable as a consequence of the constraint, which likely suppresses dissociation and (ii) the constraint may make further stabilizing interactions with the Aurora-A surface. Taken together this work unveils the first orthosteric N-Myc/Aurora-A inhibitor and provides useful insights on the biophysical properties and thus design of constrained peptides, an attractive therapeutic modality.
abstract_zh: 以N-Myc(61-89)为起始模板，我们展示了通过截短和马来酰亚胺约束的系统性方法，开发针对N-Myc/Aurora-A蛋白-蛋白相互作用（PPI）的拟肽抑制剂；这是一个潜在的抗癌药物发现靶点。其中最有前景的抑制剂——N-Myc(73-94-N85C/G89C-mal)——通过荧光各向异性竞争实验、圆二色谱（CD）和核磁共振（NMR）实验观察到，与线性野生型序列相比，其更倾向于形成符合Aurora-A结合的构象集合。进一步通过分子动力学（MD）模拟对该肽在Aurora-A结合状态下的计算机研究暗示：（i）由于约束作用，结合构象更稳定，这可能抑制解离；（ii）该约束可能进一步与Aurora-A表面形成稳定相互作用。综合来看，这项工作揭示了首个正构N-Myc/Aurora-A抑制剂，并为约束肽的生物物理特性及其设计提供了有益见解，这是一种有吸引力的治疗模式。
